title: Leaked access key on GitHub
summary: Contain a leaked credential, investigate activity, and recover safely.

triage.text: A repository scan reports an active cloud access key committed to a public GitHub repository.

choices.label: Revoke the key immediately, then preserve evidence
choices.feedback: Revocation limits ongoing abuse while preserving enough context for investigation.

choices.label: Investigate first and leave the key active
choices.feedback: Investigation matters, but leaving an exposed credential active increases the blast radius.

choices.label: Delete the repository and assume the issue is solved
choices.feedback: Deletion does not remove copies or stop a valid credential. The key must be revoked.

audit.text: The key is revoked. What should you review next?

choices.label: CloudTrail or the provider's equivalent audit log
choices.feedback: Audit logs reveal actions, source locations, and timing for the exposed identity.

choices.label: Only the GitHub commit timestamp
choices.feedback: The commit timestamp is useful context but does not show cloud activity.

scope.text: Logs show the key accessed storage and identity APIs. How do you contain impact?

choices.label: Review permissions and revoke or restrict dependent access
choices.feedback: Permission review identifies the blast radius and removes unnecessary paths to further compromise.

choices.label: Grant the key administrator access for easier investigation
choices.feedback: Increasing privileges during an incident is unsafe and expands the blast radius.

rotate.text: The key was used by a deployment job. What follows containment?

choices.label: Rotate dependent secrets and update the job through a secret manager
choices.feedback: Dependent credentials may also be exposed and must be replaced without returning secrets to source control.

choices.label: Reuse the revoked key in a private branch
choices.feedback: A revoked credential should not be reused, even in a private branch.

report.text: The technical response is complete. What closes the incident?

choices.label: Write a post-incident report with timeline, impact, controls, and actions
choices.feedback: A concise report preserves learning and assigns follow-up controls.

choices.label: Close the ticket without documenting the cause
choices.feedback: Undocumented incidents are harder to learn from and repeat more easily.

deadend.text: The response created additional risk. End the scenario and review the safer path.

choices.label: Restart the exercise
choices.feedback: Review the containment-first sequence before trying again.

title: Unexpected privileged assignment
summary: Investigate privileged access drift across an Azure environment.

start.text: An Entra ID group receives a privileged role unexpectedly.

choices.label: Preserve audit evidence and remove the unexpected assignment
choices.feedback: Containment and evidence preservation should happen together.

choices.label: Ignore it until the next monthly review
choices.feedback: Unexpected privileged access is time-sensitive.

review.text: The assignment came from an automation identity.

choices.label: Review its workload identity permissions and deployment history
choices.feedback: The source must be fixed, not only the resulting assignment.

choices.label: Disable all automation permanently
choices.feedback: Broad disruption may be unnecessary; identify the exact faulty path first.

choices.label: Add a policy check and alert on privileged role changes
choices.feedback: Preventive and detective controls address recurrence.

choices.label: Document the issue without adding a control
choices.feedback: Documentation alone does not prevent another drift event.

choices.label: End review
choices.feedback: Return to the beginning and contain unexpected privilege promptly.

title: Audit activity spike
summary: Triage unusual activity in Google Cloud audit logs.

start.text: Audit logs show a sudden increase in data access from a service identity.

choices.label: Validate the identity, source, and requested data scope
choices.feedback: Context distinguishes a valid deployment from abuse.

choices.label: Delete the project immediately
choices.feedback: Destructive action can destroy evidence and interrupt legitimate services.

contain.text: The source is outside the expected deployment network.

choices.label: Disable or restrict the identity while preserving logs
choices.feedback: Contain the suspicious principal without destroying evidence.

choices.label: Allow it because the requests are successful
choices.feedback: Successful requests can still be unauthorized.

choices.label: Rotate dependent secrets and document indicators
choices.feedback: Recovery must remove related credential risk and preserve indicators.

choices.label: Close the alert without a review
choices.feedback: Closing without review leaves the root cause unresolved.

end.text: The project was deleted before evidence was preserved.

choices.label: End scenario
choices.feedback: Review evidence-preserving containment.

title: Untrusted image in the build
summary: Respond to a container image that bypassed the expected supply-chain controls.

start.text: A production deployment references an image digest absent from the approved registry.

choices.label: Stop promotion and verify provenance and scan results
choices.feedback: Promotion gates should prevent an unverified artifact from reaching production.

choices.label: Deploy it quickly and scan later
choices.feedback: Post-deployment scanning does not prevent initial exposure.

fix.text: The image has no signed provenance.

choices.label: Rebuild from a trusted source and require signing in CI
choices.feedback: The pipeline should establish provenance before deployment.

choices.label: Allowlist the digest manually without review
choices.feedback: A manual exception needs strong evidence and expiry.

choices.label: Enforce registry, signing, and policy checks at deployment
choices.feedback: Multiple controls reduce the chance of a bypass.

choices.label: Rely on developer memory
choices.feedback: Human memory is not a reliable deployment control.

choices.label: End scenario
choices.feedback: Review the promotion gate sequence.

title: Evidence gap before an audit
summary: Close a logging and retention gap before a control review.

start.text: A control review finds that administrator activity is not retained for the required period.

choices.label: Record the gap, preserve available evidence, and assign remediation
choices.feedback: A transparent exception with evidence and ownership is auditable.

choices.label: Backdate a control statement
choices.feedback: Falsifying evidence is unacceptable and creates a larger compliance issue.

plan.text: The team can enable centralized audit retention.

choices.label: Define retention, access, integrity, and alerting requirements
choices.feedback: Retention is only one part of trustworthy audit evidence.

choices.label: Store logs in an unprotected shared folder
choices.feedback: Shared storage can permit tampering or unauthorized access.

close.text: How should the exception be reported?

choices.label: Report scope, dates, risk, owner, and target completion
choices.feedback: Clear scope and accountability support informed risk decisions.

choices.label: Omit it from the report
choices.feedback: Omission prevents responsible risk treatment.

choices.label: End scenario
choices.feedback: Return to transparent evidence handling.
